extracted.intended_audience: improv and sketch performers/writers (Second City students, alumni, and instructors)
extracted.subtask_short: Second City sketch and improv training
extracted.subtask_description: Pedagogical guidance and evaluative criteria for ensemble improv and sketch-writing for Second City mainstage shows, emphasizing group-driven discovery, live workshopping, and show-level structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes, And
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree and add — the origin point of the phrase in modern improv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use agreement to accept offers and build on them rather than negating; this is a foundational improvisational stance in Second City pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring a Brick, Not a Cathedral
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make modest, specific contributions that others can easily pick up and expand rather than trying to impose a large, fully-formed idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Your Partner Look Good
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize moves that set up and highlight fellow performers; avoid playing for personal spotlight at the expense of the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play to the Top of Your Intelligence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray characters as thinking and capable people; letting characters be intelligent often makes absurd situations funnier and clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery Over Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Find what's true in the scene rather than imposing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let comedic material emerge from honest exploration and discovery in the moment instead of forcing contrived jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open with a High-Energy, Broadly Accessible Sketch
rubrics_metrics.description: Start the show with a sketch that is energetic and easy for audiences to grasp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an opener that hooks a wide range of audience members and establishes tone and momentum for the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchor Mid-Show with a Set Piece
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor mid-show with a sustained piece (a 'set piece') that develops a single idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a longer, developed sketch in the middle of the lineup to deepen the show's arc and give audiences a payoff from sustained development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close with a Callback Sketch
rubrics_metrics.description: Close with a sketch that callbacks earlier material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a closing sketch that references or resolves earlier jokes/themes to create cohesion and a satisfying finale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Blackouts to Bridge Sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: Blackouts (10–15 second jokes) bridge between longer sketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert short, punchy blackouts to maintain pace and reset energy between longer pieces; they should be tight and immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop on Stage; Iterate with Audience Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketches are workshopped on stage, not in rooms; audience reaction across multiple performances drives revision; a sketch becomes 'set' only after dozens of performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize live testing and iterative revision informed by audience responses; expect substantial evolution before a piece is considered stable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth-in-Comedy (Funny Comes From Truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: The funny is in the truth, not the joke — played seriously, absurdity becomes funnier; played for the joke, truth becomes thinner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to honor the truthful instincts of a scene; privileging 'truth' strengthens comedic payoff and character choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did the scene EMERGE through ensemble play?
rubrics_metrics.description: Second City working rubric question assessing whether the scene arose from collaborative ensemble interaction rather than individual scripted turns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an evaluative prompt: look for scenes where ideas and beats are discovered collectively in performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did each player make the others look good?
rubrics_metrics.description: Second City working rubric criterion emphasizing ensemble support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether performers set up and elevated each other instead of undermining or stealing focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was the comedy played at the top of intelligence?
rubrics_metrics.description: Second City working rubric criterion asking if the comedic choices treated characters as competent/aware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that performances avoid playing characters as incompetent purely for easy laughs and instead honor smarter, clearer choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was the truth honored before the joke?
rubrics_metrics.description: Second City working rubric criterion ensuring truth precedes punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether scenes establish truthful circumstances and character actions before foregrounding the joke; if truth is sacrificed, the humor can feel thin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has the sketch survived multiple audiences?
rubrics_metrics.description: Second City working rubric criterion about durability through performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a sketch holds up and improves across repeated performances and revisions guided by audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the show structure breathe (long, short, long)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Second City working rubric criterion evaluating overall show pacing and variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the balance of long and short pieces across a show to ensure dynamic pacing and audience engagement.
